story.what_it_does: Force Motors is a vehicle maker. It sold 37,619 vehicles in FY2025-26, up from 32,068 the year before, and it reports a 70% share in the Traveller segment (marked 'not stated' in the notes).
story.plans: The notes contain no financial guidance. The decks only set green and social targets: 50% renewable electricity by 2027, a 50% cut in emissions intensity by 2030, and 32 employee training hours by 2030. The annual report shows R&D capital expenditure of ₹19,194 lakhs.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a moat directly. The one hint is the 70% Traveller segment share, though its source is unclear, and a 23.72% annualized ROIC for FY26 suggests the business earns good returns on capital.

scenarios.story: Vehicle sales and revenue keep growing, as FY26 revenue rose to about ₹9,05,654 lacs from ₹8,07,123 lacs. Strong returns (ROIC 23.72%) and a clean unmodified audit opinion support the view that the business is healthy.
signals_to_watch: Year-on-year sales growth after the 6% shown in Q1 FY27
Annualized ROIC staying near the 23.72% level seen in FY26

scenarios.story: Sales keep growing at a moderate pace, as in Q1 FY27 when sales rose 6% and PAT rose 14%. Profit growth is steadier because the FY26 boost from the tax regime shift and the exceptional item will not repeat.
signals_to_watch: Standalone PBT growth versus the 1% in Q1 FY27
Whether later decks report volume and EBITDA margin

scenarios.story: Profit growth stalls as PBT growth was only 1% in Q1 FY27, and the earlier jump in profit was partly one-off. Unresolved items such as the technology-transfer arbitration and the capitalised product development costs could also become problems.
signals_to_watch: Any update on the arbitration with the technology transfer counterparty
Product development cost capitalisation, flagged as a key audit matter
